in_hebrew.name: פילימון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פילימון הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו אהוב ומקובל היטב. השם נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'פhileo' שפירושה לאהוב ומ'מון' שפירושה מקובל. השם פילימון מוזכר בברית החדשה, בספר פילימון, שהוא אחד מהאפיסטולות של פאולוס.

in_greek.name: Φιλήμων
in_greek.long_meaning: Φιλήμων είναι ένα όνομα ελληνικής προέλευσης που σημαίνει αγαπητός. Το όνομα προέρχεται από το συνδυασμό των λέξεων 'φιλέω' που σημαίνει αγαπώ και 'μῶν' που σημαίνει περισσότερο. Ο Φιλήμων ήταν ένας από τους αποδέκτες των επιστολών του Παύλου, συγκεκριμένα της Επιστολής προς Φιλήμονα.

in_latin.name: Philemon
in_latin.long_meaning: Philemon nomen est originis Graecae, quod interpretatur amabilis vel acceptus. Nomen derivatur ex vocibus Graecis 'phileo' (amare) et 'mōn' (magis). Philemon fue uno de los destinatarios de las epístolas de Pablo, en concreto de la Epístola a Filemón.

in_english.name: Philemon
in_english.long_meaning: The name Philemon originates from the Greek words 'phileo' meaning to love and 'mon' meaning more. It signifies a person who is loving, friendly, and well-received. Philemon is a biblical name, being the recipient of one of Paul's epistles in the New Testament. The name conveys a sense of affection and amiability.

biblical_reference.note: The Epistle to Philemon is one of the Pauline epistles.

data.cultural_impact: The name Philemon carries a significant cultural impact in the ancient Greek and Christian traditions. In ancient Greek culture, the name was associated with those who were loved and revered for their kindness, hospitality, and wisdom. This made Philemon an esteemed and respected name among the Greeks. In the Christian context, Philemon is remembered as a bishop who embodied the virtues of kindness, hospitality, and love, making the name synonymous with the Christian values of compassion and generosity.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Philemon holds deep spiritual significance. According to the New Testament, Philemon was a Christian bishop who had welcomed and cared for Paul in his home during Paul's travels. The letter of Philemon, written by Paul, commends Philemon for his generosity and kindness and implores him to receive Onesimus, a runaway slave who had returned to Philemon, as if he were Paul himself. This act of forgiveness and reconciliation is a powerful symbol of the Christian message of love, forgiveness, and redemption. Therefore, the name Philemon is a reminder of the power of love, kindness, and forgiveness to transform lives and bring people together in unity and harmony.
